## 3. Focus: gray plus one color

Viridis colors five continents. If the message is about one continent, gray plus one color serves better.

```{r}
#| label: focus
here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  mutate(highlight = continent == "Africa") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = highlight)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text_repel(
    # Label the three most populous African countries
    data = \(d) d |> filter(highlight) |> slice_max(population, n = 3),
    aes(label = country), size = 4, color = "gray20", show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "firebrick", "FALSE" = "gray70")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## 4. Viridis against gray plus one color (5 minutes)

| Use | When |
|---|---|
| Viridis | The chart shows a variable with several groups or a numeric scale. |
| Gray plus one color | The message is about one group. |

**Your turn:** Make both versions of the Rosling 2007 chart: one with viridis for all continents, one with gray plus one color for Europe. Which one answers the question "How far behind is Africa?" Which one answers "How do the five continents compare?"

```{r}
#| label: turn-focus
#| eval: false
here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  mutate(highlight = continent == "___") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = highlight)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "___", "FALSE" = "gray70")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```
